```text
# PR #3088: Patch: the AI prices what a sleeping card does when it wakes

Closes #3064

The practice AI now counts what a Dormant card's "When this awakens" does: Imprisoned Cosmality's 10 split damage and Imprisoned Ship Smith's Fiery Waraxe. It counts this for its own sleepers and for the enemy's. Two of the issue's acceptance items are met only in a nearer form, because no sound weight can meet them as written (see Decisions).

## What changed

- **`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`**: a new probe, `awaken_prices`, runs once at the decision's root on a sandbox copy. It wakes each Dormant card that has a wake trigger, then wakes the same card with its text switched off, and prices the difference in its controller's evaluation.
  - It looks at the seat's field, then the enemy's, then the Units in the seat's own hand (each placed on the field first).
  - The price travels in a new `Prices.awakenings` field.
  - `slumber_worth` now adds `w.awaken × price` inside the same slumber share as the body.
  - `fire_turn_hook`'s body moved into a shared `settled_after`, so the wake runs under the same pool hold and random stream as a turn hook.
- **`config.rs`**: a new weight, `EvalWeights.awaken`: 1.0 in `AI_EVAL`, 0 in `GREEDY_EVAL`. A new node cap, `AI_AWAKEN_PROBE_NODES` = 16, drawn from the decision's budget. When no card has a wake trigger, the probe spends no node.
- **`decide.rs`**: calls `awaken_prices` beside the other root prices.
- **Tests**: seven `r3064000_…` tests in `crates/ai/tests/ai/slumber.rs`.
- **Docs and spec**: the AI README, §9.9, one clause in §6.1's Dormant row, the new ruling note `spec/rulings/R3064000.md`, an "Amended by" line in R2380000, and `spec/pending/3064.md`.

## How I tested it

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --check` | ok |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai -- r3064000 turn_hook` | 30 passed |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` | 786, 97 (7 daily tests ignored, as before) and 26 passed |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts` | 487 passed (5 ignored), 31 passed, and the rest passed |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-server --features …` | 1718, 670, 207 and the rest passed |
| `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo jackioh spec check` | "1699 rulings, 4148 proofs, 51123 citations in 3282 files, 21872 links: ok" |
| `cargo jackioh patches check`, `catalog check` | ok |
| `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) at `awaken` 1.0 | 20, 19 and 20 of 20 against random, greedy, and Hard vs Easy (floors 17, 10, 16); slowest decision 120 ms against a 1500 ms limit |
| `cargo jackioh gate` at `awaken` 0 | 20, 19 and 20 of 20 |

- **Mutation checks** (not committed): at `awaken` 0.0, five of the seven tests fail; the no-trigger and hidden-card tests still pass, as they should. At 0.5, both `decide` tests fail. With the evaluation asserts taken out, at both 0 and 0.5 Medium ends its turn instead of playing a lone Ship Smith, and plays the Felinor Token over Cosmality.
- **`classify`**: on uncommitted work it reads HEAD and says `Internal`. Run against a temporary unreferenced commit object (`--head <sha>`, nothing in the worktree or index touched), it says `classify: Ai`. `--claims` stops with "--claims needs --parent-bin: stage 1 left ai unchecked"; CI's `rust (classify)` runs that second stage itself.
- **No patch fragment**: an AI change claims no card family.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **Nearer forms of two acceptance tests.** The issue asked for Ship Smith over a 1-mana vanilla and Cosmality over a vanilla 2-drop, which no sound weight can satisfy.
  - The textless 1- and 2-drops are Mr. Vanilla (1) 4/4, Spikey Steven (1) 5/2 and Greaser (2) 7/7. A played one counts in full, while a sleeper counts at a quarter share, so beating one would need a weight of about 4.
  - Shrinking the rival with a stat override would skew its hand price.
  - So the tests check the nearest forms: a lone Ship Smith at one crystal is played only with the price, and Cosmality is played over a Felinor Token only with the price. A person may want different tests.
- **Weight 1.0, not the usual untuned 0.5.** The slumber share already discounts the wait, and nothing can stop a Dormant card from waking. At 0.5 both `decide` tests fail. A training screen may retune it.
- **§6.1 edited too.** The plan left §6.1's Dormant row alone, but it said the AI counts a sleeper only "as the unit it wakes as", which is now incomplete, so I added one clause citing R3064000. The pending paragraph says it edits §6.1 and §9.9.

## Worth a second look

- `AI_AWAKEN_PROBE_NODES` = 16 is new and untuned. Each probed card costs 2 nodes, or 3 to 4 for a hand Unit.
- The probe wakes every card on the AI's own turn, so an enemy Ship Smith's Waraxe enters unanimated. The ruling note states this.
- A wake that ends the game, such as a lethal Cosmality split, is not priced, the same as with the other probes. Cosmality's price is one roll on the copy's random stream.
- `shadow_ban.rs` and `generation.json` are untouched. The daily shadow-ban sweep may move for these two cards.
```

````text
# #3064: Patch: the AI prices what a sleeping card does when it wakes
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Two Stinkyscape cards fall asleep when played and do something big when they wake. Imprisoned Cosmality splits 10 damage among the enemies, and Imprisoned Ship Smith hands out a weapon. The practice AI counts such a sleeper only as the body it will wake into, so it rarely plays one and barely reacts when you play yours. Once this is built, the AI also counts the wake-up payoff, for its own sleepers and for yours.

## Why

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:680-701` (`slumber_worth`, R2380000): a Dormant card is worth `share * unit_worth` of the same card awake.
- The wake trigger (`crates/engine/src/slumber.rs:123-130`, `when_this_awakens`) is never priced, and no file in `crates/ai/src` names it. `evaluate.rs:246-249` (`has_turn_hook`) prices only the start- and end-of-turn hooks.
- The two cards are `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c019_imprisoned_cosmality.rs` and `c017_imprisoned_ship_smith.rs`.
- `training/history/sweep-2026-10-29-4.md:236-239`: Ship Smith was played 3 times in 159 affordable turns at Easy and 3 in 129 at Hard; Cosmality 2 times in 208 and once in 219. That sweep predates #2412's body price, so the gap left is smaller.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/slumber.rs:200` shows Cosmality played only when it is alone in hand.

## Proposal

- At the decision's root, as the Death, turn-hook, activation and attack-hook prices are computed, within a named probe-node budget:
  - for each Dormant card on either field that has a wake trigger, and each Dormant unit in the seat's own hand, wake it on a sandbox copy with `slumber::awaken_card` (`slumber.rs:69`);
  - price it as the controller's evaluation after waking, less the same waking of a twin without the trigger, as `attack_hook_prices` does.
- The price travels in `evaluate::Prices`. `slumber_worth` adds a new `awaken` weight times the slumber share times that price, and `GREEDY_EVAL` keeps the weight at 0.
- It reads only both fields and the seat's own hand, so hidden cards change no decision.
- A ruling note amending R2380000, with its tests and its §11 paragraph. The smoke-gate numbers go in the `config.rs` comment, as with the earlier prices.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `config.rs` and `decide.rs`.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/slumber.rs` and `crates/ai/README.md`.
- §9 (the practice AI), `spec/rulings/` and `spec/pending/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A sleeping Cosmality scores above the same body without its wake trigger, and an enemy one scores below it.
- [ ] At Medium and Hard, on two cursors, `decide` plays Ship Smith over a 1-mana vanilla and Cosmality over a vanilla 2-drop.
- [ ] Two states that differ only in hidden cards give the same decision.
- [ ] `GREEDY_EVAL` scores are unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` passes at smoke size, and the pull request records its numbers.

## Size and risks

About 5 files and 250 lines. Label it hard, since it is the AI. Only two cards print the trigger today, so a training screen may read even. Cosmality's split damage rolls on the copy's random stream, so the probe prices a single roll. The probe's nodes come out of the decision's budget.

   - In `GREEDY_EVAL`, after `attack_hook: 0.0,`, add `awaken: 0.0,`.
   - After `AI_ATTACK_HOOK_PROBE_NODES`, add `pub const AI_AWAKEN_PROBE_NODES: usize = 16;`. Its doc comment says what the nodes pay for:
     - two wakes (the card's and its hookless twin's) per Dormant card with a wake trigger on either field, and per own hand Unit with one;
     - a spawn more per hand Unit: one node, two on a full unit row.

2. **`evaluate.rs` imports and `Prices`.**
   - Add `GameEventType`, `awaken_card` and `is_slumbering` to the `jackioh_engine::{…}` import, and `AI_AWAKEN_PROBE_NODES` to `crate::config::{…}`.
   - In `Prices` (~L228), add `pub awakenings: Vec<AwakenPrice>,` after `attack_hooks`.
   - In `Prices::NONE`, add `awakenings: Vec::new(),`.
   - Add R3064000 to the R-lists in the doc comments of `Prices` and `evaluate_priced`.
   - Nothing else breaks: every other `Prices` literal uses `..Prices::default()`, and every test `EvalWeights` uses `..AI_EVAL`.

3. **Price reader.** Insert these after `attack_hook_price` and before `unit_worth`, each with an R3064000 doc comment:
   - `pub type AwakenPrice = ActivationPrice;`, keyed by definition, face and controller, as `AttackHookPrice` is.
   - `fn has_wake_trigger(state: &GameState, card: &CardInstance) -> bool`, whose body is `script_of(state, card).triggers.iter().any(|trigger| trigger.on.contains(&GameEventType::Awakened))`.
   - `fn awaken_price(state, unit, w, prices) -> f64`: a copy of `attack_hook_price` with three changes: `w.awaken`, `prices.awakenings`, and the guard `Some(price) if has_wake_trigger(state, unit)`.

   `script_of` returns a sleeper's own script: only a `vanilla` card or a set card gets the empty one (`engine/src/scripts.rs:347`). A sleeper's triggers are switched off in `triggers.rs:352` instead.

4. **`slumber_worth`** (~L700).
   - The last line becomes `share * (unit_worth(state, &awake, w, prices) + w.awaken * awaken_price(state, unit, w, prices))`.
   - Add to its doc comment: "R3064000: plus `awaken` of what its wake trigger gives, inside the same share".
   - `GREEDY_EVAL`'s shares are 0, so it returns before the price is read.

5. **`fire_turn_hook`** (~L1346).
   - Its body becomes `settled_after(before, |sink| { queue_hook(sink, holder, hook); })`. Keep the braces and the `;`: `queue_hook` returns a value, so the bare expression fails with E0308.
   - Add `fn settled_after(before: &GameState, step: impl FnOnce(&mut EngineSink<'_>)) -> GameState` after it.
     - Its body is the old body verbatim, with `queue_hook(&mut sink, holder, hook);` replaced by `step(&mut sink);`.
     - Its doc comment cites R2477000 and R3064000 and takes the pool-hold, random-stream and rule-4 sentences from `fire_turn_hook`'s.

6. **The probes.** Insert after `attack_hook_prices`, before `NextSwing`'s doc comment. `awaken_card` pushes `Awakened` onto `sink.events`, and `settle` dispatches it (`dispatch_new_events`).
   ```rust
   /// R3064000: `before` after its Dormant card wakes (`awaken_card`) and `settled_after` drains its
   /// trigger. One node: `None` when refused; `Some(None)` on a panic (`note_sim_panic`), an open prompt
   /// or a finished game, which the probe neither answers nor prices.
   fn wake_once(before: &GameState, instance_id: &str, counter: &dyn NodeCounter) -> Option<Option<GameState>> {
       if !counter.take() {
           return None;
       }
       let woken = catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
           settled_after(before, |sink| {
               awaken_card(sink, instance_id);
           })
       }));
       match woken {
           Ok(after) => Some((after.pending.is_none() && after.result.is_none()).then_some(after)),
           Err(payload) => {
               note_sim_panic(counter, payload.as_ref());
               Some(None)
           }
       }
   }

   /// R3064000: the controller's evaluation after `unit` wakes on `before`, a sandbox (R923000), less after
   /// its hookless twin wakes (text given back before scoring, `with_text_back`), plus
   /// `AI_EVAL.next_turn_mana` per crystal gained over the twin. Signed. Two nodes.
   fn awaken_probe(before: &GameState, unit: &CardInstance, counter: &dyn NodeCounter) -> Option<Option<f64>> {
       let owner = unit.controller;
       let Some(hooked) = wake_once(before, &unit.id, counter)? else {
           return Some(None);
       };
       let (twin, printed) = hookless_twin(before, unit);
       let Some(plain) = wake_once(&twin, &unit.id, counter)? else {
           return Some(None);
       };
       let plain = with_text_back(plain, &unit.id, &printed);
       let gained = hooked.players[owner].mana.current - plain.players[owner].mana.current;
       Some(Some(
           evaluate(&hooked, owner, NextSwing::Enemy, &AI_EVAL) - evaluate(&plain, owner, NextSwing::Enemy, &AI_EVAL)
               + AI_EVAL.next_turn_mana * f64::from(gained),
       ))
   }

   /// R3064000, R923001: `awaken_probe` for a Unit in `seat`'s hand, placed first (`spawn_hand_unit`); one
   /// that does not enter Dormant prices nothing.
   fn spawned_awaken_probe(world: &GameState, seat: PlayerId, card: &CardInstance, counter: &dyn NodeCounter) -> Option<Option<f64>> {
       let Some((placed, unit)) = spawn_hand_unit(world, seat, card, counter)? else {
           return Some(None);
       };
       if !is_slumbering(&unit) {
           return Some(None);
       }
       awaken_probe(&placed, &unit, counter)
   }

   pub fn awaken_prices(world: &GameState, seat: PlayerId, counter: &dyn NodeCounter) -> Vec<AwakenPrice> {
       if AI_EVAL.awaken == 0.0 || world.pending.is_some() || world.result.is_some() {
           return Vec::new();
       }
       let field = [seat, seat.opponent()]
           .into_iter()
           .flat_map(|player| units_on_field_of(world, player))
           .filter(|unit| is_slumbering(unit) && has_wake_trigger(world, unit))
           .map(|unit| (unit, false));
       let hand = world.players[seat]
           .hand
           .iter()
           .filter(|card| card_type_of_face(world, &card.def_id, card.radiant) == CardType::Unit && has_wake_trigger(world, card))
           .map(|card| (card, true));
       let mut candidates: Vec<(AwakenPrice, &CardInstance, bool)> = Vec::new();
       for (card, in_hand) in field.chain(hand) {
           if !candidates.iter().any(|(key, _, _)| key.is_for(card)) {
               candidates.push((AwakenPrice::key(card), card, in_hand));
           }
       }
       if candidates.is_empty() {
           return Vec::new();
       }
       let mut sandbox = world.clone();
       sandbox.sandbox = Some(true);
       for player in PLAYER_IDS {
           sandbox.players[player].auto_end_turn = Some(false);
       }
       let probes = create_sub_counter(counter, AI_AWAKEN_PROBE_NODES);
       let mut priced = Vec::new();
       for (key, card, in_hand) in candidates {
           let probed = if in_hand {
               spawned_awaken_probe(&sandbox, seat, card, &probes)
           } else {
               awaken_probe(&sandbox, card, &probes)
           };
           match probed {
               None => break,
               Some(None) => {}
               Some(Some(price)) => priced.push(AwakenPrice { price, ..key }),
           }
       }
       priced
   }
   ```
   Give `awaken_prices` a doc comment like `death_prices`'s. It says:
   - it probes `world`, the probe world (R185), and prices each card once, in this order:
     - the seat's Dormant field cards with a wake trigger;
     - then the enemy's (their status is public), each as its controller's;
     - then the seat's hand Units with one, placed first (R923001);
   - it never reads the enemy's hand;
   - it runs on a sandbox (R923000) with automatic turn end off (R345) and no price passed;
   - it spends at most `AI_AWAKEN_PROBE_NODES` nodes, and none without a candidate.
````
